description: A musical clock built around bars: a time signature, a tempo, and six subdivisions each with its own swing, put out both swung and on the grid

params.text: Sets the tempo in quarter notes per minute, 30 to 300
Sets the top of the time signature, 1 to 16
Sets the bottom of the time signature: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32
Starts and stops the clock on each press
Returns the bar count and the position within the bar to the top on each press, and fires the reset output
Shifts that subdivision's off-beats late or early, -50 to 50 per cent; the setting is taken up at the end of each bar rather than mid-bar

inputs.text: Changes the tempo, added to the BPM knob at about 27 BPM per volt, or read as an absolute tempo at a hundredth of a volt per BPM when the menu says so
Changes the top of the time signature, added to the numerator knob; by default the change takes effect at the next bar line
Changes the bottom of the time signature, added to the denominator switch; by default the change takes effect at the next bar line
A high gate runs the clock, taking the run button's place
Takes the tempo from the time between pulses on this jack and phase-locks the whole grid to it; the pulses per quarter note are set on the menu, and MIDI clock is always 24
Changes that subdivision's swing, added to its trimmer; the setting is taken up at the end of each bar
A rise returns the bar count and the position within the bar to the top and is passed on to the reset output

outputs.text: A trigger at the start of every bar, always on the grid because the bar has no swing
A trigger on each quarter note, with that subdivision's swing applied
A trigger on each eighth note, with that subdivision's swing applied
A trigger on each sixteenth note, with that subdivision's swing applied
A trigger three times per quarter note, with that subdivision's swing applied
A trigger three times per eighth note, with that subdivision's swing applied
A trigger whenever the reset button is pressed or the reset jack rises, for restarting sequencers together with the clock
A trigger on each quarter note at exact grid spacing, whatever the swing trimmer is set to
A trigger on each eighth note at exact grid spacing, whatever the swing trimmer is set to
A trigger on each sixteenth note at exact grid spacing, whatever the swing trimmer is set to
A trigger three times per quarter note at exact grid spacing, whatever the swing trimmer is set to
A trigger three times per eighth note at exact grid spacing, whatever the swing trimmer is set to

notes: with an external clock patched, a mismatched pulses-per-quarter setting cannot be guessed: the readout turns orange and reads PPQN? while the module runs from its own BPM knob
placing a MeterX immediately to the right gives a 24-pulse clock, a run gate and bar-length triggers taken from this module
menu: External Clock PPQN — a label over the pulses-per-quarter choices below it, which say how the external clock jack is to be read
Behavior — a label over the three choices below it
Apply time signature changes immediately — takes a new time signature at once rather than waiting for the next bar boundary
Reset on play — makes the run button and the run gate restart the bar at the top, and passes a pulse out of the reset output so downstream sequencers restart too
BPM CV absolute (0.01V/BPM — for Arrange) — reads the BPM jack as an absolute tempo at a hundredth of a volt per beat per minute instead of adding to the knob
Outputs — a label over the pulse width choice below it
Gate/trigger width — sets how long each pulse lasts: a fixed 1, 2, 5 or 10ms, or a share of that output's own period at 12.5, 25, 50, 75 or 87.5 per cent
